notices.html: Luminocity Dino Safari is closed for the season: the Freehold pop-up ran July 1 through August 16 only, so skip a special trip there until it returns, most likely next summer.
Last weekend for Bellemont Farm's Sunflower Festival: it wraps up Sunday September 13, so advance online tickets ($19 adult, $12 kids) beat the door price ($25, $15) if you want to catch it.

blurbs.terhune: This weekend: Fall Family Fun Weekends opens for the season, Saturdays and Sundays 10am to 5pm through November 1, $10 per person age 3 and up, with the corn and hay maze, pony rides, pumpkin picking and live music. Apple and peach picking status after the spring freeze is still unclear, so call 609-924-2310 to check what fruit is actually ready before counting on it.
blurbs.leeturkey: This weekend: no fresh update is posted for this small, family-run farm, but with fall underway it typically means apples for pick-your-own alongside late tomatoes and other produce. Call 609-448-0629 to confirm before you head over, and note the fields close by 5:15pm.
blurbs.vonthun: This weekend: apples are ready to pick, Golden Delicious, Mutsu, Gala and Crimson Crisp, and blackberries are still going too. The full fall festival with corn maze and hayrides doesn't start until September 19, so for now it's just u-pick and the farm market. Call 732-329-8656 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.emerys: This weekend: no change from last week, u-pick blueberry season has wrapped, though fresh and frozen berries are still sold in the farm market. The corn maze and pumpkins don't open until September 26. Call 609-758-8514 to confirm before a special trip.
blurbs.battleview: This weekend: no change from last week, this year's spring freeze wiped out sour cherries, peaches, nectarines and apples, so there's no pick-your-own fruit right now, just the country store and bakery. Pumpkin picking and hayrides usually start in late September but no exact date is posted yet. Call 732-462-0756 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.johnsons: This weekend: apple and pumpkin picking are in full swing after the Apple of My Eye Festival kicked off the season on September 6, with hayrides running continuously 10am to 5pm. Weekend admission is $11.99 per person and includes the hayride, paid at the Farm Stand. Call the Pick Your Own Hotline 609-654-5894 to check on the Sunflower Celebration, which may be winding down this late in the season.
blurbs.dinosafari: This weekend: Luminocity Dino Safari has closed for the season, it only ran through August 16, so there's nothing to visit here right now. It typically returns next summer, so check back closer to then.
